sections.html:
Howard County is in north central Indiana. Kokomo is both the county seat and the largest city, and Greentown, Russiaville and Indian Heights are the other communities people name most often. The county covers 293.92 square miles, and the 2020 census counted 83,658 residents, with about 74 percent living in areas counted as urban.

Manufacturing, automotive work in particular, is the backbone of local employment. Stellantis runs a transmission plant, the Indiana Transmission plants and a casting plant here, a Kokomo engine plant started production in 2022, and StarPlus Energy, a joint venture of Stellantis and Samsung SDI, is in town as well. Many households rely on a handful of plants, so plant news moves housing demand.

Tornadoes are part of the local record. An F4 tornado struck the south side of Kokomo on April 11, 1965 and killed 25 people in the area. Two tornadoes hit the north side on April 20, 2004. On August 24, 2016, an EF3 tornado damaged about 1,000 homes on the south side and destroyed 80.

Kokomo gets about 44.4 inches of precipitation and 34.1 inches of snow in an average year. If your house has old storm damage, a roof near the end of its life or a repair that was never finished, it will show up in an appraisal and in a buyer's inspection. Fix it or be ready to price it in.

Three offices in the Howard County Administration Center, 220 North Main Street in Kokomo, share the work, and all keep weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

  • Assessor, 765-456-2211: assessed values, Form 130 appeals and exemption applications on Form 136. The assessor also acts as secretary to the county Property Tax Assessment Board of Appeals.
  • Auditor, 765-456-2215 (tax line 765-456-2216): homestead deduction filings and tax sale listings.
  • Treasurer, Room 226, 765-456-2213: bills, payments, delinquent lists, and weed, demolition and nuisance liens.

The treasurer takes payments online through InvoiceCloud, at four local banks and in a drop box to the right of the Administration Center entrance. Partial payments are accepted. For a reassessment question, call the assessor, who is working through eastern Howard County starting with Taylor Township.

Certified rates for taxes payable in 2026 run from about 1.80 in rural Clay Township to about 3.75 inside the Kokomo city district that overlaps Taylor Township. Each rate is stated per $100.00 of taxable property.

Tax districtTotal rate per $100.00
Clay Township1.7992

Kokomo City, Taylor Township3.7452

More than twenty districts exist, so match the district code on your tax bill to find yours.

The rate is only part of the story, because Indiana limits what a parcel can owe as a share of gross assessed value.

  • 1 percent for a homestead that receives the homestead standard deduction
  • 2 percent for other residential property, including single-family houses that are not homesteads and buildings with two or more dwelling units
  • 2 percent for agricultural land and 3 percent for nonresidential and personal property

The homestead standard deduction is shrinking on a schedule set by 2025 legislation: $48,000 for the 2025 assessment date, $40,000 for 2026, $30,000 for 2027 and $0 from 2030 on. A supplemental homestead deduction grows over the same years, starting at 40 percent for taxes payable in 2026 and reaching 66.7 percent in 2031.

A homestead application must be completed and dated by December 31. You do not reapply each year unless the property is sold, the title changes or the contract is paid off. For a buyer, that means the seller's deduction does not carry over automatically.

Start with a Form 130 filed with the assessing official, one petition per parcel. The deadline is June 15 of the year tied to the notice. If the county mails Form 11 before May 1, it is June 15 of that assessment year. Otherwise it is June 15 of the year the treasurer mails the bill.

After filing, the assessor schedules a preliminary informal meeting and reports the result to the county board. The board must hold a hearing within 180 days of the petition and mail notice at least 30 days ahead. If you disagree with the decision, or none arrives in 180 days, file Form 131 with the Indiana Board of Tax Review.

Two details help owners. The assessor carries the burden of proof if the value rose more than 5 percent over the prior assessment date, unless the jump came from renovation, new improvements or a change in use. And while an appeal is pending, you may pay on the previous year's assessment without penalty until it is resolved.

Installments are due each May and November. Late payments carry a 5 percent charge if paid within 30 days (on a parcel with no back taxes), and the charge rises to 10 percent of the unpaid tax after that.

Indiana bills a year behind. The bill you pay reflects ownership and value as of January 1 of the prior year, which is why a mid-year closing can leave a buyer paying a prorated share of the seller's arrears. Your closing agent sets the exact split.

sections.h2: Unpaid taxes and the tax sale
sections.html:
Parcels with delinquent taxes go to an annual tax sale in the Commissioners' Meeting Room, which may move to an online auction. A property cannot sell for less than the delinquent taxes and special assessments, the taxes due in the sale year, penalties, $25 for postage and publication, and related county costs. The owner can still redeem after the sale:

  • 110 percent of the minimum bid if redeemed within six months, or 115 percent after that
  • Plus any overbid amount and 5 percent yearly interest on it, plus taxes the buyer paid afterward
  • For certificates sold at the 2026 sale, the redemption period ends October 27, 2027. Certificates struck to the county may end February 24, 2027.

A parcel comes off the certified list when the taxes are paid in cash, by cashier's check or by credit card.

sections.h2: What to gather before selling with tax due
sections.html:
Collect the paper that shows exactly what is owed before you talk to any buyer. The treasurer can tell you the amount due on a parcel, and a closing agent pays it from proceeds.

  • Your latest tax bill and the parcel number
  • Any Form 11 assessment notice and any Form 130 you filed
  • Whether the parcel appears on the certified tax sale list
  • Records of weed cut, demolition or nuisance liens the treasurer has placed
  • Your homestead deduction approval, if you claimed one

Confirm every figure by phone before you rely on it. A cash sale can close without repairs or financing delays, and the tax is still paid from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Who sends the property tax bill in Howard County, Indiana?
faqs.a: The Howard County Treasurer, at 220 North Main Street, Room 226 in Kokomo, collects property tax and can be reached at 765-456-2213. Questions about value or a missing homestead deduction go to the assessor or auditor.

faqs.q: When are Howard County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Installments are due each May and November. Partial payments are accepted, and you can pay online, at a participating bank or in the drop box.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Howard County taxes late?
faqs.a: The state's schedule adds 5 percent for payment within 30 days of the due date on a parcel with no back taxes, and 10 percent of the unpaid tax after that.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Howard County assessment?
faqs.a: File Form 130 with the assessor by June 15 of the year tied to your notice, one form per parcel. If the county board's decision is unsatisfactory, Form 131 goes to the Indiana Board of Tax Review.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Howard County house that is on the tax sale list?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying the taxes takes the parcel off the certified list, or the closing agent pays them from proceeds. After a tax sale, an owner can still redeem, and for certificates sold at the 2026 sale that period ends October 27, 2027.
